title: Natural Domain and Range of an Even Rational Function
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the real-valued function G(t) = 2 / (t^2 - 16).

steps.title: Identify Denominator Singularities
steps.explanation: Factor the denominator as a difference of squares to find the excluded values t = -4 and t = 4 where division by zero occurs.
steps.why: A rational expression is undefined at the real roots of its denominator.

steps.title: State the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: Excluding t = -4 and t = 4 divides the real number line into three open intervals.
steps.why: Puncturing the real line at two points produces three connected open intervals.

steps.title: Analyze the Range on the Exterior Intervals
steps.explanation: When |t| > 4, t^2 - 16 takes all positive values in (0, inf). Consequently, G(t) = 2 / (t^2 - 16) takes all positive real values in (0, inf).
steps.why: The reciprocal of an expression that ranges continuously over (0, inf) also ranges over (0, inf).

steps.title: Analyze the Range on the Interior Interval and Combine
steps.explanation: When |t| < 4, t^2 - 16 lies in [-16, 0), achieving its minimum -16 at t = 0 where G(0) = -2/16 = -1/8. As |t| -> 4^-, G(t) -> -infinity. Combining both branches gives Range = (-inf, -1/8] U (0, inf).
steps.why: The union of the images of all domain components forms the complete range of the function.
